entry.label: Homeostasis
entry.description: Dynamic maintenance or restoration of internal variables within viable ranges despite disturbance. It is neither immobility nor a synonym for a single feedback loop.
entry.canonical_definition: The organised maintenance of internal variables within viable ranges despite disturbance; the relevant variables, ranges, mechanisms and time scales must be specified.

profile.title: Homeostasis
profile.canonical_definition: The organised maintenance of internal variables within viable ranges despite disturbance; the relevant variables, ranges, mechanisms and time scales must be specified.
profile.summary: Homeostasis is dynamic maintenance, not stillness. A living system keeps selected internal variables within viable ranges while energy, matter and information continue to flow and conditions continue to change.
profile.why_it_matters: The idea is useful for understanding stability and resistance to disturbance. In organisations it is often used metaphorically; the metaphor only earns its keep when the variables, ranges and mechanisms being maintained are named.
key_distinctions: maintained condition vs one feedback loop
viable range vs exact set point
historical_lineage: Claude Bernard: internal milieu as precursor
cybernetics connected homeostasis with regulation and feedback
practice_connections: ask what the system is working to keep unchanged
look for hidden work that maintains dysfunction
identify who benefits from the maintained state
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
